risk_note: RV2, settlement rebate port only, no migration, no contract change, no money moves (withdraw lane, model Claude Fable 5.1; orchestrator rulings D10-864 ②, D10-875, D10-878). Before this task a jd order fully refunded before credit (quantity − refunded_quantity = 0, B1-08zi's columns) stayed ESTIMATED / WAITING unless the union reported an invalidation or the commission went to 0, so a monthly bill could still credit it. Now the rebate port's pre-credit decision reads the quantities orders wrote in the same sync transaction (the row re-read under the order lock) and, when orders.jd.refunded_quantity_r9_enabled is on, voids the order as a whole-order invalidation — event PLATFORM_INVALID through the generated transition (R6 → VOID, reason REFUND), no entries, order.invalidated on the same transaction; with the switch off (the default, as in production) it only writes one warn alert and the other rules run as before. The check is jd-only (other platforms keep null quantities), runs after the platform signals and before the commission check, and never reaches CREDITED or terminal orders. The same check runs on the first import (decideImport, after P13): a jd order whose first report is already fully refunded goes R1 / R2 then R6 → VOID in the same transaction (covered: #16, #17; switch off: #18). Real risks: voiding a credited order (covered: #12), a second invalidation of an already VOID order (covered: #13), voiding on a partial refund or a missing quantity (covered: #6, #7, #10), a partial write when the publish fails (covered: #15), cross-app switch leakage (covered: #14). Test-machine full verify not run (AWS runners disabled, D10-555; CI verify-int is the full verification, approvals 21); the red run and the implementation's runs were made in the local Docker container / host slot.
